memory_lessons.applicability: Supports a follow-up tile-size experiment, but does not establish that 512 is faster than 256.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 256-entry shared-memory tile candidate passed all 11 correctness cases and had a mean time of about 1.004 ms versus the baseline's about 1.849 ms. This evidence supports testing shared tiling, but does not isolate the cause of the timing difference or identify an optimal tile size.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 512-entry tile under the same correctness suite and timing protocol, then compare it with the measured 256-entry tile.

proposal.hypothesis: A 512-particle shared-memory tile may reduce synchronization rounds relative to the previously measured 256-particle tile while preserving the pairwise arithmetic and source order. Its larger shared-memory footprint may offset that benefit; the controller's correctness suite and timing protocol must decide.

retained: Replace the 256-entry static shared-memory source tile with a 512-entry tile while leaving the 256-thread launch settings unchanged.
Load tile entries cooperatively with a thread-strided loop and keep both block barriers unconditional so partial tiles and inactive target threads synchronize uniformly.
Preserve the source iteration order, pairwise force expression, self-interaction skip, and copied output mass.
